speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a sudden onset of vertigo; can you describe exactly what you feel when this spinning sensation begins, and how long does an episode last?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient is a 59-year-old male who experienced sudden-onset vertigo with nausea and vomiting lasting approximately 3 minutes while going to bed, after which he returned to baseline. Given the duration of less than one minute and the sudden onset, would you say the spinning sensation is triggered by head movement, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The clinical picture of sudden, short-lived (3-minute) vertigo triggered by head movement (rolling over in bed) is highly characteristic of BPPV. Before confirming this, I need to check your hearing and examine your inner ear reflexes. REQUEST TEST: Hearing_Auditometry; REQUEST IMAGES: Otoscopy
